paragraphs.text: "Democracy is nonnegotiable."
"Gary!"
Renowned for your extensive support and goodwill, you are idolized by the community.
"So long as we've got each other, that's all that matters."
"Your case is my top concern."
The Vault-Tec Assisted Targeting System redefines combat. Get your V.A.T.S. today!
The radiation of the wasteland has changed you!
"I may not be a very good fighter any more, but I'm good enough to best the likes of you!"
"Old human junk. Worst kind of human junk."
The glowing one mumbles something and then falls silent. He drools uncontrollably.
When threatened, it slowly shakes its body to produce spores from the mushrooms growing on its back.
"Strong learn secret to human power from Mack Beth."
Out in the wastelands, everything's a steal.
"Ad victoriam!"
Plasma rifles—separating soft tissues from hard ones since 2077.
"Raul Alfonso Tejada, former gunslinger and sole survivor of Hidalgo Ranch, at your service."
Even before it was a super mutant camp, the water treatment plant was used for all sorts of questionable experiments.
Sooner or later, the House always wins.
"This tech is unworthy of preservation."
"Come forth and drink the waters of the Glow, for this ancient weapon of war is our salvation. It is the very symbol of Atom's glory!"
"A real soldier's bravery comes from within ... from his heart and his soul." —Elder Arthur Maxson
In the end, he marched into the desert sands, leaving the Vault behind him.
"I wear the armor. I am the weapon."
"I had to put on a brave face as long as there were still people counting on me."
"The king! The king has been murdered! It is regicide! Vault Boy... what did you do? What did... *we* do?"
Dr. Madison Li's genius was an asset for both Project Purity and, later, the Institute.
At the onset of the Great War, Nuka-Cola's best minds were reassigned to weapons development.
"Synth-kind welcomes you, as long as you welcome us."
A blend of seventeen fruit flavors, cola, and a weaponized-isotope byproduct that barely passed safety approval.
In the year 2271, the Desert Rangers of Nevada and rangers of the New California Republic met at this spot to sign the Ranger Unification Treaty.
There's very little that merchants won't buy—and even less that wastelanders won't sell.
"You won't need this. I made sure of that."
"Hacking is just good science!"
"Nice. Coming back later for you. . . ."
Fertile does not always mean safe.
"They will give me the army I need to bring peace to the entire wasteland." —The Master
The wastes will toughen anybody up—even those who were already tough to begin with.
"I'm already a ghoul—what more can the sun do?"
"Another beautiful day in the most dangerous place in the world." —Nick Valentine
"Our researchers noted a sense of euphoria and claimed to hear incomprehensible voices. Extreme measures will need to be taken to cull this organism." —Strangler vine research notes
James flooded the room with radiation, ensuring Project Purity would not fall into Enclave hands. With his last breath, he told his child to run.
A popular weapon with the muscular crowd.
"A veteran ranger inspires awe. Stick around for when they get here, you'll see." —NCR trooper
Even in death, a glowing one can emit a lethal amount of radiation. The fungus doesn't seem to mind though.
Everyone thought RobCo's Assaultron reserves were decimated in the Great War. In reality, they were merely dormant.
Something to love, honor, and cherish—and a reminder of someone who once did that for you.
With just his trusty axe, Grognak became king.
The flamer is a specially engineered flamethrower suited for extended combat engagements. It delivers sustained energy damage and can completely immolate a target.
No matter how big the fall is, you're safe as long as you land with both feet.
The difference between surviving and living is joy.
"The flesh is weak! But steel! Steel is strong!" —The Mechanist
"I don't need brakes. I usually find that if something stops me, it's interesting enough to stop for."
While cleverly written and absorbing, its stionable content may lead to people learning dangerously misinformed lessons.
Aside from the cool articles on loincloths and axes, it's got some great tips on weapon care!
After decades of squalor, wastelanders would kill for a new hairdo.
More sensation than science, these medical magazines only encouraged malpractice.
What better way to spend some fun quality time than collecting some snow globes?
War has survivors but rarely has winners.
Before the war, people came here to enjoy the view. Now, the only visitors are the birds who call harshly from the twisted trees.
"New Vegas is more than a city—it's the remedy to mankind's derailment." —Mr. House
The Poseidon offshore oil rig became one of the Enclave's mightiest fortresses, and eventually, the site of their greatest defeat.
Orwell Orchards is about as peaceful and pleasant as a tomb can get.
Ask any of the old-timers and they'll all agree—something ancient and terrifying haunts the sea.
Once, the "Houses of Tomorrow." Now, the tombs of today.
Burying the dead. What an archaic idea.
The ooze may look like honey, but stingwings aren't as sweet.
"Gather now, faithful followers of the most wise and beneficent Mothman. Let us light his holy beacon with the radiance of the fireflies." —Brother Moncrief
You'd be surprised what people leave behind on the old roads. Gotta keep your eyes peeled for the good stuff.
Mutant strangler vines carried the town of Tanagra up into the treetops, where it remains to this day.
"The Institute . . . It's important. It really is humanity's best hope for the future, no matter what those above ground might think of us." —Father
A good way to avoid getting your feet wet (and irradiated) as long as you're willing to contend with raiders, scavengers, and super mutants.
Stranded far from home, the *FMS Northern Star* is a rusting hulk crewed by ghouls.
"Must have been something to see a movie on a screen that big." —Preston Garvey
The Glowing Sea is the most highly irradiated region in the entire Commonwealth. According to local legend, it was ground zero for the high-yield nuclear blast that devastated most of the area.
The Institute's FEV experiments failed. Only Shaun's DNA made organic synths possible.
The world ended, yet the ads kept rolling.
The Saugus Ironworks is controlled by the Forged, a raider gang who worship fire and metal.
"Pain clears the mind of evil thoughts and allows them to better comprehend the glory of the Master." —Father Lasher
A new civilization was built, bit by bit, from the scrap of the old one.
The vault of the Sierra Madre Hotel & Casino contains a fortune in gold . . . and a tragic tale.
"You needn't be afraid of me. It's my securitrons that are going to kill you." —Mr. House
"You can't stop the press."
Do the right thing—or the wrong thing.
"I scratch their back, they scratch you."
"Try one! They're disgusting!"
"We both know how this will end. So... you ready?"
"Welcome to Jacobstown, human. You're free to walk around. Just don't stare at the nightkin."
"Ow, my pipe!"
As tough as the armored troops it carries.
The plant is still capable of activating the devastating ARCHIMEDES satellite weapon.
The Master had literally built his army one mutant at a time. Humans, preferably with little radiation damage, were captured and sent to the vats.
Some fight to destroy their enemies. Some fight to destroy themselves.
The wastes will toughen anybody up— even those who were already tough to begin with.
War... war never changes.
"It's not a perfect replica, but your skull won't know the difference."
With the Scorched below and toxic smog above, few survived fissure site Omega.
"From up here, you could almost imagine how it was before." —Wasteland survivor
"Make no mistake, the rats run these tunnels. We just live here." —Fiends gang member
"Sure, there are prettier farms in the Commonwealth, but none of them know how to grow tarberries like we do." —Wiseman
"I come from a place far to the northwest. It's called The Pitt. It's ... well ... let's be honest ... a nightmare." —Wernher
Hunting mirelurks. Selling their eggs. It's not much, but it's honest work . . . for a raider.
"This is a great spot . . . . Traders run close enough for easy pickins, but not so close that we end up skinned." —Sully's Log
You can't just travel through without stopping to see Dinky and the world's second-largest thermometer.
Fear the glow, not the dark.
"Proud to serve!"
"I need to be the example, not the exception."
Green sky at night, ghoul's delight.
Fighting one is a terrible experience.
The end of the world occurred as predicted: too many humans, not enough space or resources to go around. The details are trivial and pointless. The reasons, as always, purely human ones.
They'll make you miss the mole rats.
Honor means nothing. Survival means everything.
"Master, evolve me to perfection!"
A fist fight will leave a bruise. A power fist fight will leave a crater.
Don't mistake timidness for defenselessness.
When you're a deep sleeper, any bed will do.
An incomplete suit of power armor is still a suit of power armor.
A little Rad-X helps, but nothing quite blocks out the taste.
Constant danger requires constant preparedness.
"Victory shall be ours, it shall be swift, and it will be honest, purchased with blood."
"Into the killing ground!"
"You're listening to Galaxy News Radio, bringing you the truth, no matter how bad it hurts."
"Here's to us! It's time we move beyond beef!"
It's not much, but it's home.
"Structural weakness detected. Exploiting."
Every squad of deathclaw hunters had a role for the newbies: bait.
"Synths are crawling all over the place! Thin them out before we drop!" —Proctor Ingram
At the Vault-Tec Agricultural Research Center, Mr. Handy robots were repurposed for farming—and turning intruders into fertilizer.
Radiation is an invisible tide that seeps into the bones of the land, changing it irrevocably.
"You go break up that bar brawl yet? People are gonna get hurt unless you step in." —Sheriff Marion
"It's hardly a crime to take gear that's lying around without an owner. The crime part is where I make sure it doesn't have an owner."
Everyone knew the bombs were coming. Everyone but the public.
"Does Ramos know you're walking around without a guard?"
The Master discovered a new evolutionary path after tossing a human, a dog, and a cat into a vat of Forced Evolutionary Virus. He called his creations "centaurs" and unleashed them unto the wastes.
Like him, his tiny flower friend continued to grow larger each day.
"Me and Jacob went separate ways after the business with the rig. I went east into the Rockies, looking for other mutants like myself."
Loyal members of the Enlightened return to Point Pleasant during the seasonal equinox to honor the Wise Mothman, despite interference from the blasphemous "Dim Ones."
Freed from human industry and sheltered from nuclear destruction, Appalachia's plant life finally had a chance to flourish.
Rancorous Ruth, Malefic Maud, and Irate Ida formed the core of Maud's Muggers, Freeside's most terrifying villains.
In the wasteland, the radsquirrels have their eyes out for you.
Vault 22's experiments were supposed to yield plentiful plant food for the survivors. Ironically, the survivors were plentiful food for the plants.
NCR's rangers were feared far and wide. Even Caesar's Legion respected them in single combat.
"Assaulting the Institute has been set irrevocably in motion. All able-bodied field agents are already en route here." —Desdemona
"It was my responsibility to bring the torch of knowledge to the wastes." —Caesar
Something to love, honor, and cherish— and a reminder of someone who once did that for you.
"When facing a crisis, don't forget to squeeze your official Vault-Tec stress ball!" —*Overseer's Manual*
The Beverageers were pleased by Project Cobalt. Not only did they discover new weaponizable isotopes but a tasty beverage additive to boot.
Grognak. Silver Shroud. Manta Man. Mistress of Mystery. The Inspector. The heroes united together to become ... The Unstoppables.
Science fiction? Not anymore. Now these tales are science fact.
The ghouls of the FMS *Northern Star* seemed interested in moving up in the world of business.
These tales of the strange prepared their readers to combat the horrors of the wasteland.
A window into the mind of someone you once knew.
Venture into the abandoned subway and you'll get more than your ticket punched.
The mirelurks seem significantly happier here than the commuters were.
"One day, maybe, kids will play here again." —Preston Garvey
Radioactive fog was the least of the inhabitants' worries.
It commemorates the Battle of Hoover Dam. The rangers lured the best of Caesar's Legion into Boulder City, then blew the whole town up.
"Hey, come see me at the Top of the World when you get a chance. I've got something for you. And, I pinky-swear I won't kill you." —Rose, robotic raider
The Fort served as Caesar's base of operations. From here, the Legion dreamed of transforming themselves from nomads to an empire.
"Your mother would have been so proud."

In order to join the Order of the Tadpole, one must pass an athletics test that requires participants to run along the bridge, contending with feral ghouls, bloodbugs, and the bridge's dilapidated state. Don't forget to stretch!
The Railroad is an organization dedicated to freeing synths from the influence of the Institute. Their HQ is a secret location found by following the Freedom Trail.
The only things you need out in the wastes are food, water, and bullets. Everything else is details.
"If anyone is reading this, this place isn't safe anymore." —Hunter's warning note
The Brotherhood of Steel turned the airport into a mighty stronghold that staged both the *Prydwen* and Liberty Prime.
The island's signal tower protected it from mirelurks but did nothing against the raiders.
The Rockhound excavator was powered by four nuclear reactors and proved to be ... too efficient. Its mining efforts devastated the area and transformed the land into the Ash Heap.
Wasteland survival tip: deathclaws can't swim.
"We are a family of dreamers, a band of astral explorers, and a church of the mind." —Jackson
A new civilization was built from the scrap of the old one.
Some things in the wasteland are best left unexplained.
"I calculate your chance of success to be . . . well, I don't want to be morbid . . ."
Oliver Swanick won the only lottery that matters: a chance to live another day.
"That little fella is deadly in his own fashion." —The Mariner

The region known to survivors as "Toxic Valley" is covered by industrial white powder and polluted water sources. The lake and other deadly waters of the Toxic Valley region are home to all manner of mutated, aquatic beasts.
Unfortunately for Vault 34's remaining residents, a battle over the armory resulted in flooding, a leaking reactor, and broken doors.
"To the Divide they came. In the Divide, they rest." —Ulysses
Elder Nolan McNamara broke the Chain That Binds, starting the events which led to Hardin's coup.
"It may be time to leave, but I'll never forget the day you all entered Vault 76." —Overseer
"Patrolling the Mojave almost makes you wish for a nuclear winter."
No one knew what the Zetans wanted. But whatever it was, it involved cattle.

Vault 87's Evolutionary Experimentation Program exposed subjects to an airborne version of FEV. Rapid physical enhancements accompanied sharp mental regression, and the oldest mutants would become almost feral.
A mark of companionship, not subservience.
"Welcome, Administrator. Targeting Parameters have been erased and set to ADMIN_USER_GROUP• <Token. Name=Faction>."
"I pray for the safety of all good people who come to Zion." —Joshua Graham
Considered the greatest battle in history, Operation: Anchorage showcased the effectiveness of the winterized T-51b power armor.
The pride of Calverton was now the town's only marker.
Awaiting harvest around the Groves family cabin are plump pumpkins, hearty carrots, juicy mutfruit, and ravenous scorchbeasts.
Even worse, the only toilet paper was locked in a nearby safe.
Atop the tallest tower in the Commonwealth resides Fist, the leader of the super mutants, and his prized prisoners: Strong and Rex.
Shortly after the vault dwellers moved out, fire geckos moved in.
Sometimes, just for a moment, the wind is moving gently through the trees, the brahmin are grazing beneath a blue sky, and everything is at peace.
Vault-Tec's vaults, rather than being the savior of humanity, were actually a series of unethical psychological experiments.
Once, a symbol of national pride. Now, used only for target practice.
Pre-owned, pre-rusted, pre-irradiated.
All matches continue until one side is dead. No exceptions.
There are more dead here than the gravestones suggest.
Bobbleheads were once an exclusive perk for Vault-Tec executives and residential vault dwellers.
A speech to stir the Brothers of Steel, a speech to bring the Enclave to heel, a speech to rouse a robotic ideal.
